key_points: Weeve removes names and addresses from text before users submit it to AI assistants.
The tool is free, requires no download, and takes only seconds to process information.
Weeve offers free transcription services in 25 languages for recordings up to 60 minutes long.
The company's primary product is a local-first AI note taker that keeps meeting data on the user's laptop.
items.summary: Weeve provides free tools to help users avoid sharing private information with artificial intelligence assistants. The Dutch startup offers a service that removes identifying details from text before AI processing. Weeve also provides free transcription in 25 languages and a local-first AI note taker for Mac. These features allow users to analyze documents securely without leaking personal data to public databases.
items.title: Weeve offers free privacy tools for safe AI data use

This release marks a substantial increase in scale from the previous Hy3 model.
items.summary: Tencent introduced Hy4 Preview, a new open-weight text-only large language model. The model features 770 billion total parameters and a 1 million token context window. It offers two reasoning effort levels: high and no_think. The release represents a significant increase in size compared to the previous Hy3 model.
items.title: Tencent launches Hy4 Preview, a massive 770B parameter open-weight LLM

key_points: Vijay Pande co-founded VZVC with Zach Werner to focus on concentrated biotech investments.
The new firm targets approximately five investments per year instead of dozens.
Biological data cannot be scraped like text, limiting AI training opportunities.
Clinical trials remain costly despite AI advancements in drug discovery.
Pande seeks founders with high integrity who prioritize long-term partnerships.
items.summary: Vijay Pande, formerly of a16z, co-founded VZVC with Zach Werner to pursue a concentrated investment strategy. The firm plans to make approximately five investments annually instead of the dozens typical of larger funds. Pande explained that biology differs from text because biological data cannot be scraped from the internet, creating unique challenges for AI models. He noted that while AI improves drug discovery, clinical trials remain expensive and animal models often fail to predict human responses. Pande emphasized the need for high-integrity founders who prioritize long-term collaboration over competition. The new firm relies on AI agents for operations rather than hiring associates.
items.title: Vijay Pande launches small firm VZVC to make five concentrated biotech bets

Lawyers note a rise in AI-related labor disputes over the past few years.

key_points: The Centre for Research on Energy and Clean Air reports that the conflict between the United States, Israel, and Iran increased global energy import costs by $330 billion between March and August.
The European Union suffered the most financial pain, paying an extra $78 billion due to its reliance on foreign oil and gas.
China and India followed as the next largest affected importers, paying additional $35 billion and $22 billion respectively.
The International Energy Agency estimates that hostilities have knocked out 9.6 million barrels of daily refining capacity in the Middle East.
items.summary: The Centre for Research on Energy and Clean Air reports that the conflict between the United States, Israel, and Iran increased global energy import costs by $330 billion between March and August. The European Union suffered the most financial pain, paying an extra $78 billion due to its reliance on foreign oil and gas. China and India followed as the next largest affected importers, paying additional $35 billion and $22 billion respectively. While crude oil accounted for the largest share of extra costs, liquefied natural gas prices in Asia remain 75% higher than pre-war expectations. The International Energy Agency estimates that hostilities have knocked out 9.6 million barrels of daily refining capacity in the Middle East. Low-carbon energy sources like wind and solar provided a partial offset by saving importers $36 billion during the period.
items.title: Iran War Adds $330 Billion to Global Energy Import Bill

key_points: Illinois Governor JB Pritzker signed SB 3484 into law to regulate high-speed electric bikes.
The new rules require 40 mph e-bikes to be registered, titled, and insured like motorcycles.
Vehicles must comply with federal motor vehicle safety standards to be eligible for registration.
Most existing high-powered e-bikes lack the required manufacturer certifications for legal road use.
items.summary: Illinois Governor JB Pritzker signed SB 3484 into law, creating a legal pathway for high-speed electric bikes on public roads starting January 1, 2027. The legislation treats electric motor-driven cycles with speeds up to 40 mph as motor vehicles, requiring registration, titling, insurance, and a valid driver's license. However, the law mandates that these vehicles must comply with federal motor vehicle safety standards and possess a legitimate vehicle identification number. Most current high-powered e-bikes lack the necessary manufacturer certifications and documentation to meet these requirements. Consequently, while the state offers a regulatory framework for these devices, the majority of existing models cannot be legally registered or operated on public roads under the new rules.
items.title: Illinois legalizes 40 mph e-bikes but requires motorcycle registration

key_points: Coal supplied 72.5% of Polish electricity in 2021 but fell to 52.7% by 2025.
Renewables generated more electricity than coal in June 2025 for the first time.
Poland allowed high-emitting coal plants to participate in 2026 capacity auctions under a special exemption.
The IEA forecasts Polish renewable generation will reach about 53% of total generation by 2030.
items.summary: Poland's electricity transition is accelerating, with coal's share of generation dropping from 72.5% in 2021 to 52.7% in 2025. Renewables reached 31.4% of generation in 2025, surpassing coal for the first time in June. Gas generation also grew significantly, contributing 24.4 TWh in 2025 alongside wind and solar. Despite falling generation, Poland maintains high-emitting coal capacity through a special derogation in its capacity market auctions. The International Energy Agency expects renewables to overtake coal annually by 2028. Poland faces a dual challenge of reducing energy mix reliance while building the grid infrastructure needed to replace coal's reliability functions.
items.title: Poland rapidly reduces coal use while retaining high-emitting capacity for reliability

key_points: The California Air Resources Board assigned a historic low carbon-intensity rating to a biogas-to-hydrogen project at Bar 20 dairy farm in Kerman.
Environmental groups criticize the project for prioritizing carbon credits while ignoring local water and air pollution from dairy waste lagoons.
CARB officials stated the low rating reflects the capture of methane emissions that would otherwise enter the atmosphere.
Experts note that converting biogas to electricity and then hydrogen results in energy losses compared to direct biogas utilization.
items.summary: A dairy farm in Kerman, California, is operating a new biogas project that converts methane waste into hydrogen fuel. The California Air Resources Board assigned the project the lowest carbon-intensity rating in the state's history, sparking debate among environmental groups. Critics argue the project prioritizes climate metrics over local water and air pollution caused by dairy waste lagoons. While regulators highlight the project's potential to displace fossil fuels, environmental advocates contend that carbon credits incentivize herd expansion and mask ongoing contamination issues. The facility, Bar 20, has faced previous citations for runoff and groundwater monitoring failures. CARB officials maintain the low rating reflects the capture of methane that would otherwise enter the atmosphere, though they note the approval is provisional. The project supplies hydrogen to refueling stations via truck, despite broader market challenges for hydrogen fuel. Experts warn that energy losses during conversion reduce the total fuel yield compared to direct biogas use. This case illustrates the tension between state climate goals and local environmental justice concerns surrounding industrial agriculture.
items.title: California Dairy Farm Gets Record-Low Carbon Rating for Biogas-to-Hydrogen Project

key_points: Pennsylvania spends approximately $180 million annually on waste coal subsidies under the AEPS regulation.
The state currently generates more energy from waste coal than from solar arrays, ranking 42nd in renewable energy production.
House Bill 501 seeks to downgrade waste coal in the energy portfolio but has stalled due to intra-party political opposition.
Industry leaders warn that reducing subsidies could cause waste coal plants to close, halting the removal of legacy pollution piles.
Costs for the waste coal program increased roughly 13-fold between 2020 and 2025 after the state mandated in-sourcing.
items.summary: Pennsylvania continues to spend millions subsidizing waste coal burning despite the state's renewable energy generation ranking 42nd nationally. The Alternative Energy Portfolio Standards (AEPS) regulation mandates utilities purchase specific fuel sources, with waste coal currently providing about 3 percent of the state's energy compared to 4 percent from renewables. Critics argue these subsidies hinder climate progress, noting that burning waste coal produces significantly more greenhouse gas emissions than traditional coal plants. Although House Bill 501 aims to reduce waste coal's role and increase renewable requirements, the proposal has stalled in the Democrat-controlled State House. Political opposition comes from both Republicans and a faction of Democrats representing coal regions who fear plant closures. Industry representatives warn that altering subsidies could force specialized plants into precarious 'peaking' modes, potentially ending cleanup operations. Meanwhile, costs for the program have risen sharply since 2020 border restrictions required in-state waste coal. Environmental advocates suggest creating a separate state program to manage waste coal, but lawmakers remain divided on the best path forward.
items.title: Pennsylvania Subsidizes Coal Waste While Renewables Lag Behind

key_points: Global pure electric vehicle registrations rose 16% year-over-year to 1.8 million units in July.
The Tesla Model 3 deliveries crashed 44% year-over-year, dropping to 11th place globally.
Leapmotor doubled its sales year-over-year to reach six-digit levels and overtook Hyundai-Kia.
Toyota set a new record with 50,415 registrations, narrowing the gap with Volkswagen.
Excluding China and the USA, global EV sales jumped 50% year-over-year in July.
items.summary: CleanTechnica reports that global pure electric vehicle registrations reached 1.8 million units in July, representing a 16% year-over-year increase. While battery electric vehicles (BEVs) grew significantly, plugin hybrid sales declined by 11%, causing the overall plugin market to rise only 7%. BEVs accounted for 71% of all plugin sales in July, marking the highest share since 2022. The Tesla Model 3 saw deliveries crash 44% year-over-year to 19,000 units, falling to 11th place globally, whereas the Tesla Model Y remained the top-selling model despite a 9% drop. BYD's Song secured second place, aided by exports and a new generation, while a group of small EVs from Geely and BYD filled the third through seventh spots. Leapmotor achieved record sales, doubling its output year-over-year to reach six-digit levels and surpassing Hyundai-Kia to take sixth place among manufacturers. Toyota also set a new record with 50,415 registrations, edging closer to Volkswagen in the legacy OEM rankings. The article notes that excluding China and the USA, EV sales jumped 50% year-over-year in July.
items.title: Global EV sales surge in July as Tesla Model 3 drops and Leapmotor rises

The deal allows Nvidia to influence developers to use its chips instead of competitors' processors.
Hugging Face generates about US$150 million in annual revenue, resulting in a high sales multiple.
The acquisition may undermine the open-source AI movement's goal of decentralising power.
items.summary: Nvidia has reportedly agreed to acquire Hugging Face for US$13 billion, a deal that would significantly expand the chipmaker's influence over open-source AI development. The article notes that Hugging Face previously rejected a US$500 million investment from Nvidia in 2024 to avoid concentration of power. This transaction occurs as OpenAI develops custom chips that could compete with Nvidia's hardware. By owning Hugging Face, Nvidia aims to steer developers toward its processors rather than those from competitors like Google. The startup generates approximately US$150 million in annual revenue, making the purchase price roughly 86 times its annualised revenue. Critics argue this move creates a paradox where a company promoting open models may instead strengthen its own market dominance.
items.title: Nvidia reportedly agrees to buy Hugging Face for US$13 billion

key_points: The CMA removed disclosure requirements for multinational companies owning local vet clinics.
Pet owners pay 16.6% more on average at large vet groups compared to independent practices.
The Progressive Veterinary Association has threatened a judicial review over softened ownership disclosure rules.
More than 60% of veterinary practices are owned by six major groups including private equity investors.
items.summary: The Competition and Markets Authority (CMA) removed requirements for multinational companies to disclose which veterinary practices they own, raising concerns that pet owners could be misled. The CMA found that pet owners pay 16.6% more on average at large vet groups than at independent practices within the £6.3bn market. While new rules propose capping prescriptions at £21, the Progressive Veterinary Association (PVA) has threatened a judicial review after the CMA softened wording to allow corporations to obscure ultimate ownership. The PVA argues this allows large groups to hide behind misleading brand names, whereas the CMA believes recognisable high street names are more useful to consumers. More than 60% of practices are currently owned by six major groups, including private equity investors and Mars Petcare.
items.title: CMA vet ownership rules change risks pet owners being misled by private equity firms

items.summary: Iceland has rejected the government's proposal to hold accession talks with the European Union, public broadcaster RUV reported. The "No" camp secured 52.5 percent of votes while the "Yes" camp received 47.5 percent. Prime Minister Kristrun Frostadottir had previously stated that a "No" would end all EU speculation. Campaigners argued that membership could lower interest rates but also threatened sovereignty and fishing waters. Iceland first applied to join the EU in 2009 during a financial crisis.
items.title: Iceland rejects EU membership plan in referendum

The movement of roughly 60 million tonnes of rubble into Israel and the West Bank introduces heavy metals and pathogens to local environments.
Environmental experts warn that chemical contaminants in shared aquifers could degrade water quality for agriculture and drinking over time.
items.summary: The article reports that untreated sewage and contaminated rubble from Gaza are creating significant environmental hazards for Israel. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and the Board of Peace recently agreed to form a working group on sanitation, though its structure remains undisclosed. Daily sewage flows from Gaza into the Mediterranean, causing desalination plant shutdowns and toxic algae blooms that impact Israeli coastal waters. Additionally, the transfer of approximately 60 million tonnes of rubble into Israel and the West Bank risks spreading heavy metals and pathogens to local populations. The text notes that while groundwater contamination is less likely, chemical salts pose long-term risks to shared aquifers. Environmental groups warn that ignoring these shared ecological boundaries endangers Israeli citizens just as it does Palestinians.
items.title: Toxic waste from Gaza war now threatens Israeli public health

key_points: Lonely Planet ranks ten global destinations for autumn foliage, spanning six continents.

Wildlife viewing and wine tasting are highlighted as key attractions in several locations.
items.summary: Lonely Planet has released a ranking of the ten best destinations worldwide for viewing fall foliage, covering locations across six continents. The list highlights how autumn colors vary by region, with Northern Hemisphere sites peaking in October and Southern Hemisphere locations like Chile and Tasmania displaying colors in April or May. Wine regions such as Burgundy and Ticino feature prominently, while wildlife viewing remains a key attraction in parks from Alberta to the Scottish Highlands. Travelers are advised to plan carefully, as many sites require renting a car and booking months in advance. Specific recommendations include the Adirondacks for water-based leaf peeping, Alberta for golden larch groves, and the Iya Valley in Japan for remote gorges. The guide also notes that timing is critical, as peak color windows can shift by several days depending on weather conditions. Each entry provides practical advice on transportation, accommodation, and local activities tailored to the unique landscape of that destination.
items.title: Lonely Planet ranks ten global destinations for autumn foliage viewing

More than a third of Chinese billionaires have held or sought formal political office, according to political science analysis website Good Authority.
One in five Russian billionaires has sought or held political office, according to Good Authority.
The line between economic and political power is steadily eroding as the influence of wealthy individuals over governments becomes more pronounced.
items.summary: John P. Ruehl reports that the United States is leading a global trend where ultrawealthy businessmen hold significant political influence. The article notes that the Trump administration includes 57 cabinet members and senior officials with net worths exceeding $100 million. Ruehl explains that this surge taps into an anti-establishment mood while shrinking the permanent bureaucracy elevates political appointees. The author compares this American phenomenon to China, where more than a third of billionaires have held political office, and Russia, where oligarchs remain embedded in politics despite Kremlin control. Ruehl argues that the fusion of business and government affects geopolitics as major firms operate global infrastructure foreign governments depend on. The article concludes that as business and political disputes overlap, commercial infrastructure can become a target in geopolitical conflicts.
items.title: US Billionaires Increasingly Merge Business and Political Power Globally

key_points: A European Broadcasting Union investigation revealed a WhatsApp group facilitated hundreds of millions of euros in cash transfers for crime and extremism.
Belgian magistrate Vincent Guerra described the 'Traders of Greater Europe' network as a vast, professional system covering the entire planet.
The group chat was uncovered during a 2024 Belgian court case that convicted six money launderers, including network head Abu Adam.
Police found evidence suggesting at least 12,000 transactions were processed using photos of banknotes and identity cards as identifying codes.
Europol officials identified the hawala system as the primary money-laundering channel for organized crime, including human trafficking and drug trafficking.
items.summary: An investigation by the European Broadcasting Union found a WhatsApp group called 'Traders of Greater Europe' was used to move hundreds of millions of euros via the hawala system. The 532-member chat, containing over 82,000 messages, arranged cash transfers for organized crime and extremism without a paper trail. Belgian magistrate Vincent Guerra described the network as professional and global, noting it funded the Islamic State and facilitated people smuggling. The cache of messages was obtained after a 2024 Belgian court case convicted six money launderers, including network head Abu Adam. Police discovered evidence of at least 12,000 transactions, supported by thousands of photos of banknotes and identity cards. While hawala is legal in the UK for registered brokers, it remains illegal in most of the EU. Authorities in Austria also dismantled rings using the system for human trafficking and torture. Europol officials state the hawala system is the primary money-laundering channel for organized crime across Europe.
items.title: WhatsApp group facilitated hundreds of millions in cash transfers for crime

key_points: Erin Brockovich has launched a platform to monitor the environmental impact of AI data centers run by Meta and Google.
Experts describe her activism as an example of ecofeminism that values lived experience and community knowledge.
Scholars argue her work demonstrates how citizens can challenge corporate power without formal academic credentials.
Activists and philosophers state that society needs more figures like Brockovich to address ecological and civilizational crises.
items.summary: Erin Brockovich, the woman who won a landmark lawsuit against Pacific Gas & Electric, has turned her activism toward Big Tech. She has launched a reporting platform to track the environmental impact of artificial intelligence data centers operated by companies like Meta and Google. Experts argue her work exemplifies ecofeminism and validates the legitimacy of lay knowledge over academic credentials. Alicia H. Puleo, a philosopher, states that Brockovich defends the Earth and rejects androcentric authority. Eva Saldaña of Greenpeace Spain notes that women's leadership often stems from their structural position in society regarding care work. Alfredo Menéndez Navarro, a professor, explains that Brockovich's approach represents a democratization of knowledge where communities investigate risks. Charles Barthold, a lecturer, suggests younger generations can learn perseverance and justice from her practice. The article concludes that society needs more role models like Brockovich to challenge indifference and protect the future.
items.title: Activist Erin Brockovich now challenges Meta and Google over data centers

items.summary: Researchers at the Minneapolis Federal Reserve report that artificial intelligence demand and President Donald Trump's tariffs are similarly elevating US core inflation. While tariff impacts on clothing and footwear have become visible, the report suggests core inflation would remain one percentage point above the Fed's 2 percent target even without tariffs. The analysis highlights that AI investment boom effects currently outweigh potential future tariff pass-throughs in many sectors.

items.summary: The Delhi Development Authority (DDA) has released a set of FAQs detailing the provisions of the Master Plan for Delhi 2047 (MPD-2047). The DDA clarified that existing approved plans remain valid, while new norms apply to additional Floor Area Ratio (FAR) or revised plans. Key updates include minimum plot sizes for redevelopment, voluntary participation in transit-oriented development policies, and a new land pooling framework where landowners may retain up to 60% of pooled land. items.summary: The article details how North Carolina missed an opportunity to resolve hog waste pollution following the 2000 Smithfield Agreement. Although the deal mandated the replacement of outdated lagoon systems with environmentally superior technologies, Smithfield Foods refused to adopt the available solutions. Critics argue the industry successfully manipulated the definition of economic feasibility to avoid costly upgrades that would protect public health. The article notes that Smithfield has since grown into a global giant, yet its local operations remain reliant on the same primitive waste management systems that caused environmental disasters in 1996 and 1999.
items.title: North Carolina Failed to Fix Hog Pollution Despite 2000 Agreement

items.summary: A decade-long study in Zambia demonstrates that teaching young women negotiation skills significantly improves their long-term economic prospects. Professor Corinne Low explains that the curriculum focused on understanding others' perspectives rather than viewing negotiators as enemies. Recently, the NGO Free to Run adapted the material for online classes in Afghanistan, helping 1,200 girls navigate restrictions imposed by the Taliban. While systemic change remains necessary, these skills offer a practical way for women to manage their interests within current patriarchal structures.

items.summary: Iceland voted 52.8% to 47.2% against resuming European Union accession negotiations, effectively ending membership talks. The article identifies four main takeaways from the referendum. Second, a stark urban-rural divide emerged, with only the two Reykjavík constituencies voting yes while rural areas voted no. Third, Icelanders chose to maintain their current status under the European Economic Area, which grants single market access while excluding fisheries. Finally, the result highlights that wealthy nations like Iceland calculate EU membership differently than poorer candidates who view it as essential for growth. Prime Minister Kristrún Frostadóttir stated that voters are satisfied with the existing agreement.
items.title: Icelanders reject EU accession talks in referendum by narrow margin

key_points: Kanupriya Dhingra distinguishes between the Delhi Amrita Pritam lived in and the Delhi she wrote about in her fiction and poetry.
Pritam resided in Delhi for 58 years, working at All India Radio and editing the magazine Nagmani from her Hauz Kaus home.
Her literary works often portrayed the city as a place of decay, isolation, and gendered oppression rather than a sanctuary.
The convergence of her lived and written experiences occurred when her house was demolished five years after her death.
Dhingra argues that while Pritam's physical address was erased, her literary legacy survives through translations and secondhand copies.
items.summary: Kanupriya Dhingra explores the distinct relationship between writer Amrita Pritam and Delhi, distinguishing the city she inhabited from the one she depicted in her work. Pritam lived in Delhi from 1947 until her death in 2005, working at All India Radio and editing the literary magazine Nagmani from her Hauz Khas home. While the city eventually honored her with an honorary doctorate and Rajya Sabha nomination, her writings frequently indicted Delhi as a place of sickened values and isolation. The two versions of the city converged only when her son sold and demolished her house five years after her death. Dhingra notes that Pritam's poem 'Mera Pata' renounces a fixed address, a stance the city eventually mirrored by erasing her physical home.
items.title: Amrita Pritam lived in Delhi but wrote about a different city

key_points: Positive AI sentiment among US workers fell from 81 percent in 2019 to 43 percent by mid-2026 according to Glassdoor.
Gen Z women represent the most skeptical workforce demographic with only 21 percent of their AI-related comments being positive.
Managers remain the most optimistic group, whereas insurance claim adjusters and customer service representatives view AI almost entirely negatively.
Fear of job loss is the single most common complaint, accounting for 20 percent of negative reviews.
items.summary: A Glassdoor analysis indicates that positive sentiment regarding AI among US workers dropped from 81 percent in 2019 to 43 percent by mid-2026. The report highlights significant demographic divides, noting that Gen Z women are the most skeptical group with only 21 percent positive comments. While executives remain optimistic, roles like insurance claim adjusters and customer service representatives view AI almost universally negatively. Fear of job loss accounts for 20 percent of negative reviews, though many workers also complain about forced adoption and unrealistic productivity expectations. The data suggests that once a role encounters moderate AI exposure, criticism appears regardless of actual automation threats.
items.title: Glassdoor analysis shows US worker sentiment toward AI has sharply declined

key_points: The author predicts US gas cars will lose transportation value by 2031 as cheap used EVs become available.

Several factors like charging access and truck availability could delay the predicted value collapse in the US.

items.summary: The author reports a five-year prediction that ordinary gasoline and diesel cars in the US will become worth less than zero as transportation by 2031. Norway effectively ended new internal combustion engine sales in 2025, while China saw used gasoline car values drop significantly as electric vehicle adoption surged. items.title: India's 7% growth may fall short of Modi's 2047 developed nation dream

Broadcaster ABC called the by-election for Herdegen, marking a significant shift from last year's results where Labor won the area. items.title: One Nation party wins Western Australia special election seat

items.summary: The article reports that residents of Narsarsuaq, a remote settlement in southern Greenland, are increasingly concerned about the potential return of United States military presence and the exploitation of local natural resources. items.title: Residents fear US military return and mining threats in southern Greenland

items.summary: Arthur Kermalvezen and Audrey, both donor-conceived in Paris, fell in love but feared they might be half-siblings due to limited sperm banks. items.title: Donor-conceived couple in France tests for sibling relation

items.summary: Hindusthan National Glass and Industries (HNGIL) has issued a default notice to B9 Beverages for alleged unpaid dues of ₹11.77 crore. The notice claims the brewer failed to lift over 51 lakh customised glass bottles manufactured against confirmed orders. HNGIL stated that these branded bottles cannot be sold to other buyers, causing severe financial hardship. B9 Beverages now has 10 days to pay or record a dispute before HNGIL approaches the National Company Law Tribunal. Suraj Mehta, Chief Strategy Officer at HNGIL, said the company remains open to a resolution while the matter is under legal consideration. B9 Beverages has been out of production since September 2025 and carries an estimated debt of around ₹1,000 crore. Anicut Capital is leading the restructuring process alongside existing shareholders.
items.title: HNGIL issues default notice to B9 Beverages over unpaid glass dues

items.summary: A catastrophic flash flood on August 26 killed 734 people and left over 3,000 missing in Nepal after a rock and ice collapse triggered a debris flow. The disaster destroyed critical infrastructure along the China-Nepal border and revealed a lack of sustained trans-boundary cryosphere data sharing between India and China. While Nepal mobilized its own rescue forces quickly, the event underscored the dangers of episodic glacial failures that cannot be tracked by rainfall alone. The article argues that India and China must establish a joint Himalayan Glacial Hazard Early Warning System and a pre-authorized humanitarian assistance compact to prevent future tragedies. Without open-source, glacier-specific data sharing, local residents and tourists remain vulnerable to these compound disasters.
items.title: Flash Flood in Nepal Highlights Need for India-China Data Sharing

key_points: US government debt has reached a record $40 trillion, increasing fears that high inflation will hurt stock returns and purchasing power.

items.summary: US government debt has reached a record $40 trillion, raising concerns that high inflation could erode investor purchasing power over the next decade. Tom Essaye, founder of Sevens Report Research, warns that instead of a market crash, investors may face a scenario where stock portfolios remain stable in nominal terms while inflation destroys their real value. Essaye notes that policymakers might allow inflation to reduce the real burden of debt rather than implementing painful spending cuts or tax increases. He points to the period between 1966 and 1981 as an example where high inflation caused real portfolio values to fall by around 50%. Essaye suggests investors consider shorter-term bonds, Treasury Inflation-Protected Securities, and companies with strong pricing power to protect against this risk.
items.title: US debt hits $40 trillion: Why high inflation could cause a ‘lost decade’ for stocks

items.summary: RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat addressed a crowd at Madison Square Garden for an event organized by AHEAD, drawing both enthusiastic support and significant opposition.
